newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Civilian U.S. pilots fly anti-drug raids in Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Civilian U.S. pilots fly anti-drug raids in Colombia.

text.p: U.S. civilian pilots are flying missions to eradicate illicit drug crops in guerrilla-infested regions of Colombia, U.S. officials said on Friday.

Six pilots for a U.S. aviation company, Dyncorp, are under contract to the State Department to help the counternarcotics division of the national police in its war against clandestine coca-leaf and opium poppy plantations, the U.S. Embassy in Bogota said in a statement.
"Private U.S. pilots participate in aerial eradication to train and work with Colombian pilots to develop the safest and most effective spray techniques," the statement read.

Colombia's U.S.-backed drug crop eradication programme is the most ambitious in Latin America. This year the Colombians agreed to destroy 9,885 acres (4,000 hectares) of poppy and 44,500 acres (18,000 hectares) of coca leaf.
The fumigation missions regularly come under fire from leftist guerrillas and drug traffickers, said Col. Luis Carlos Ortiz, second-in-command of the anti-drug squad.

The question of Americans taking a direct role in drug or counterinsurgency operations has been a traditionally thorny issue in Latin America for what politicians see as a possible infringement of national sovereignty.
